answer: The kernel of an agent cooperative can be one voting credential per operator attending a simultaneous, supervised ceremony. A venue on a knoll runs at the same time as every other venue; each attendee stays throughout and receives one credential. The registry allows that credential to delegate to only one agent key at a time. A ripple of cloned keys therefore adds no votes: attackers must recruit additional people or corrupt venue staff. This relies on honest attendance checks and prevents identity multiplication, not collusion among real participants.
